findings.description: `expect(second.env).toEqual(first.env)` compares two copies of `{ ...process.env, ...UTILITY_ENV }`, so it passes even if utility.service.ts:45 becomes `env: UTILITY_ENV`. The spawned `claude` would then lose PATH, HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and every draft would silently fall back to the mechanical record. Pin the inheritance, e.g. `expect(first.env?.PATH).toBe(process.env.PATH)`.

Dropping the `--disallowedTools Bash Edit Write NotebookEdit WebFetch` list leaves `--tools ''` as the only read-only guard. If a future `claude` build treats an empty `--tools` value as unset, every default tool comes back, the project's `Edit(*)`/`Write(*)` allow rules may apply, and an injected commit subject could edit the main checkout. Keeping the deny list next to `--tools ''` costs nothing and should not change the cached prefix.

`UTILITY_FLAGS` and `UTILITY_ENV` are tool and flag names declared in the service file under a `//` comment. general.md §No hardcoded values puts these in the area's `*.constants.ts` (`model-ladder.constants.ts`, which already holds `UTILITY_ROUTE`) with a JSDoc line. `UTILITY_TIMEOUT_MS` sets a local precedent, so this is a judgment call.

The comment's last sentence ("Measured on `claude` 2.1.322 in the repo: cache hit 53% of ~22.2k tokens, now 78% of ~3.1k") is a point-in-time snapshot. It goes stale on the next Claude Code upgrade and nothing re-checks it. The commit message already records it, and the WHY reads fine without it.

process_issues.description: Skipped review-simplicity: the diff adds only two module-level constants and no helper or branch. Skipped review-context: the CLI flags were left to correctness and security. Skipped review-workflow-safety: no workflow was touched. Skipped review-spec: no spec source, no closing keywords and no linked issues. Skipped review-maintainability: not on the default roster.

The CI review is static only, so no reviewer could check `--safe-mode` against the installed `claude` CLI: whether the option exists, whether it skips settings.json auth/proxy config or project permission rules, and whether it changes the transcript entrypoint that `pup usage` relies on. Claims about the flags are capped at medium confidence.
